subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Decubitus Ulcer and Definitive Prolapse Surgery

steps.tx: Friction ulceration of the dependent cervix in long standing prolapse is the **decubitus ulcer**. The exposed cervix rubs on clothing and dries, breaking down at its lowest point. Any ulcer that looks atypical earns biopsy because cancer hides in chronic prolapse ulcers. Healing the ulcer always precedes definitive repair to keep infected tissue out of suture lines.
steps.say: A decubitus ulcer forms by friction on the dependent cervix in prolapse.

steps.tx: Reduction of the prolapse with packing and local oestrogen heals most ulcers, termed **ulcer preparation**. Atrophic postmenopausal epithelium thickens and vascularises under oestrogen cream. Surgery on an unhealed ulcer invites breakdown and fistula. Weeks of preparation are treatment, not delay, and elderly women tolerate them well at home.
steps.say: Ulcer preparation involves reduction, packing and oestrogen before definitive repair.

steps.tx: Cervical amputation with ligament plication preserving the uterus is the **Manchester Fothergill** operation. It suits uterine descent with an elongated cervix in women wishing uterine conservation. Shortening the cervix can stenose it and complicate later pregnancies. It fails when vault support itself, rather than the cervix, is the main problem.
steps.say: The Manchester Fothergill operation preserves the uterus by amputating the cervix.

steps.tx: Vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair for prolapse is the **Ward-Mayo** tradition. Removing the uterus eliminates its descent while repairs rebuild both walls. Enterocele sac excision and vault anchoring complete the operation. It remains the workhorse for postmenopausal prolapse with completed families and healed ulcers.
steps.say: Ward-Mayo vaginal hysterectomy removes the uterus and rebuilds the pelvic floor.

steps.tx: Sewing the vaginal walls together to obliterate the canal is **Le Fort colpocleisis**. It offers the highest success and shortest operation for elderly women who are not sexually active. The uterus can remain in situ behind the closure when pathology is excluded. Regret follows poor counselling, so the sexual activity question is asked explicitly and kindly.
steps.say: Le Fort colpocleisis obliterates the vaginal canal for elderly women.

steps.tx: Anchoring the vaginal vault to the sacrum with mesh is **sacrocolpopexy**. It restores vaginal length and axis better than vaginal routes for vault prolapse. Abdominal or laparoscopic access and mesh erosion are its prices. It suits younger, active women with recurrent vault descent after vaginal repairs have failed.
steps.say: Sacrocolpopexy involves anchoring the vault to the sacrum with mesh.

steps.tx: Age, sexual activity, comorbidity and prior failure choose the operation, summarised as **operation selection**. The same prolapse earns colpocleisis in one woman and sacrocolpopexy in another. Tissue quality and surgeon experience honestly belong in the discussion. Photographs and diagrams help women choose with real understanding of each trade off.
steps.say: Operation selection involves age, sexual activity and comorbidity for each woman.

steps.tx: Bladder, ureter and rectum lie millimetres from every prolapse suture, defining **repair dangers**. Cystoscopy after vault suspension confirms ureteric patency when kinking is feared. Rectal examination before closing posterior repairs finds stray sutures. Recognising injury in theatre converts a fistula into a repaired incision.
steps.say: Repair dangers involve bladder, ureter and rectum beside every suture line.

steps.tx: Vault support, wall repair and perineal rebuilding together decide durability, closing with **repair principles**. Apical suspension is the step whose omission most predicts recurrence. Early mobilisation and load advice protect healing tissues. Review at healed stage confirms anatomy before discharge from follow up care.
steps.say: Repair principles require apical suspension for durable prolapse surgery.
